payload.baseline:
THE WINNER'S MATRICES ARE THE BASELINE. Nothing is redrawn. Nine elements, each with a black-box description — what it is responsible for, what crosses its boundary, and nothing about how it does it.

E1 TREE SEARCH. Holds F1 locate, F5 bound, and the working-tree half of F2 deliver-in-portions.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: answering 'where is this, in the bytes as they are now', with the surrounding lines in the same answer, within declared caps.
  CROSSES ITS BOUNDARY: in — a pattern, a path scope, a context width, a cap. Out — matches as records, each with path, line, text and its surrounding lines, plus an explicit statement when nothing matched or when the cap truncated.

E2 RECORD SEARCH. Holds F4 reach-the-record and the ref half of F2.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: answering 'what did a named revision say'.
  CROSSES: in — a pattern, a ref, a path scope. Out — the same record shape as E1. THE SHARED OUTPUT SHAPE IS THE CONTRACT, and it is the highest-value seam in the design: a caller must not need to know which element answered.

E3 REACH. Holds F3 reach-outside and F6 contain.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: turning a declared name into an addressable source, and refusing anything that escapes it.
  CROSSES: in — a declared name and a relative path. Out — a resolved location, or a refusal naming the undeclared root.

E4 ANSWERS. Holds F7 refuse-malformed, F8 report-absence, F9 report-incompleteness.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: what a non-answer looks like, uniformly, for every lane.
  CROSSES: in — a call and its declared argument contract. Out — a refusal carrying clause, expectation, what arrived, and a remedy.
  KEPT SEPARATE FROM E1/E2 DELIBERATELY: if honesty lives inside each retrieval path, each grows its own idea of a non-answer, which is the defect where a missing argument produced a confident search.

E5 EDITS. Holds F10 alter-many-as-one, F11 guard-each, F12 undo-the-whole, F13 one-writer.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: changing the product, indivisibly, and being the only thing that does.
  CROSSES: in — a set of edits each with its own guard. Out — what changed, or which single edit failed and why, with nothing written.

E6 RULES. Holds F14 select, F15 resolve, F16 report-weight, F29 expose-the-unattached.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: handing the agent every rule that binds the step in hand, resolved to content, and naming any rule that binds nobody.
  CROSSES: in — a state identity. Out — the applicable rules as text, their volume, and the unattached set.

E7 CHECKS. Holds F17 derive-a-fact, F18 compare, F19 defer, F20 state-the-fact, F21 distinguish-computed-from-asserted, F30 refuse-an-empty-proof.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: deciding mechanically what can be decided, deferring what cannot, and marking which is which.
  CROSSES: in — a gate and the record. Out — per check: pass, fail, or defer-with-reason, each carrying the fact behind it.

E8 RECORD. Holds F22 name-immutably, F23 name-readably, F24 remove-competing-names, F25 carry-outward, F28 record-consultation, F31 preserve-what-was-superseded.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: the record outliving carelessness, and every consultation being attributable.
  CROSSES: in — a close, or a read. Out — a hash, a readable name, and a log entry naming its source.

E9 REVIEW AND DELIVERY. Holds F32 demand-the-review, F33 return-work, F34 keep-the-path-traversable, F35 withdraw-a-standing-decision, F36 deliver-the-shared-judge.
  RESPONSIBLE FOR: obliging the examination, carrying out its verdict, and making one agent's improvement to the shared judge available to all of them or to none.
  CROSSES: in — a gate submission, a verdict, or a set of engine files. Out — a form that cannot be satisfied without its rounds; a re-activated cone with the path back intact; a withdrawn offer; a promoted engine or an untouched trunk.
  WHY F33 AND F34 SHARE AN ELEMENT: the coupling is a CONTRACT, not a sequence, so splitting them fails silently. It was split by accident in the implementation and the walk deadlocked twice.
  WHY F36 SITS HERE RATHER THAN IN E8: the partitioning called it a cluster of one and filing it under preservation would hide what it is. It is not record-keeping. It is the only function whose failure makes two agents disagree about what a gate MEANS — and the review is precisely what a gate means, so it belongs beside the review.

STRUCTURE METRICS, carried from the winner unchanged: 9 elements, 14 inter-element edges, longest dependency chain 4.

SETTINGS: F26 present-settings and F27 accept-settings are allocated to E8. The partitioning named this cluster loose and named THIS as the tear, and I am recording that the tear was NOT taken: settings stay with the record rather than becoming a tenth element. The reason is that both are machine-local and neither is on any hot path; a tenth element would add an edge to buy nothing. If settings grow — more secrets, per-project profiles — that is where the split goes, and this sentence is the marker for whoever does it.
payload.allocation_exact:
EVERY FUNCTION IS ALLOCATED EXACTLY ONCE. This is a column property of the allocation matrix, checked by counting rather than by reading.

F1→E1 · F2→E1 and E2 · F3→E3 · F4→E2 · F5→E1 · F6→E3 · F7→E4 · F8→E4 · F9→E4 · F10→E5 · F11→E5 · F12→E5 · F13→E5 · F14→E6 · F15→E6 · F16→E6 · F17→E7 · F18→E7 · F19→E7 · F20→E7 · F21→E7 · F22→E8 · F23→E8 · F24→E8 · F25→E8 · F26→E8 · F27→E8 · F28→E8 · F29→E6 · F30→E7 · F31→E8 · F32→E9 · F33→E9 · F34→E9 · F35→E9 · F36→E9.
Count: 36 functions, 36 allocations. Every element non-empty. No function unallocated.

ONE APPARENT VIOLATION, and it is the only interesting row: F2 (deliver material in portions) appears against BOTH E1 and E2. That is not a double allocation — it is the SAME function realised over two sources, which is the whole point of the winning candidate. To keep the column property literally true it is recorded as F2 allocated to E1, with E2 holding the ref-scoped SPECIALISATION of it under the identical output contract.
  I am stating this rather than quietly writing 'F2→E1' because the alternative reading — that the architecture allocates one function twice — is exactly the duplication the one-implementation-per-job criterion forbids, and a reader is entitled to check that this is a specialisation and not a second implementation. The test is the shared output contract: a caller cannot tell which element answered. If that ever stops being true, this IS a double allocation and the criterion has been violated.

CHECK CLASS: review, not engine-computed. The property is mechanical and could be computed once functions and elements are nodes rather than prose — which is the same blocker that defers two lints, and it is recorded here as a third instance of one cause rather than as a separate problem.
payload.interfaces_both_ends:
THE ELEMENT MATRIX IS SYMMETRIC WHERE IT MUST BE: every interface is declared at both ends, with one meaning per edge — Ei→Ej means Ej needs something Ei produces or establishes.

THE FOURTEEN EDGES, each named at both ends:
  E1↔E2 (contract) — the SHARED RESULT SHAPE. Declared by E1 as what it emits and by E2 as what it must match. The single most important interface in the design and the one the losing candidate would have removed by having only one element.
  E3→E1 (contract), E3→E2 (contract) — both searchers accept a source resolved by reach; reach declares the resolved form, both declare that they consume it.
  E1→E4, E2→E4, E3→E4, E5→E4 (contract, four edges) — every lane's non-answers take E4's shape. Declared by E4 as the refusal form and by each lane as what it raises. This is a star rather than a chain deliberately: one idea of a non-answer, four users.
  E1→E5 (data) — you locate before you alter.
  E1→E7, E2→E7 (data) — facts are derived by retrieving material, so every check is a reader.
  E6↔E7 (contract) — THE CLAIM THE PARTITIONING CALLED STRONGEST: a rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a check must be the same rule, or the machine says one thing and checks another. Declared at both ends: E6 publishes the rule identity, E7 consumes it.
  E7→E9 (contract) — a check that can be computed is a round the agent must not be asked to assert; E9 declares which fields accept a computed verdict, E7 declares which it can supply.
  E9→E8 (data) — returning work produces superseded claims that E8 must preserve and keep addressable.
  E9→E5, E9→E8 (resource) — delivering the shared judge contends with edits and the record for the repository.

ASYMMETRY THAT IS DELIBERATE, and recorded so it does not read as an omission: E4 (answers) declares no outbound edge to anything. It is consumed by four elements and consumes none. That is correct — it is a shape, not a stage — but a symmetry check that assumed every edge must be bidirectional would flag it, so the exception is named here.

WHAT SYMMETRY MEANS HERE, since 'symmetric' can be read two ways and only one is intended: it does NOT mean every dependency is mutual. It means no interface is declared at one end only — no element consumes something no element publishes, and no element publishes something nothing consumes. Checked in both directions across all fourteen: no orphan producers, no orphan consumers.

CHECK CLASS: review, not engine-computed — same blocker as the allocation property.

DIAGRAMS: none drawn here. The guidance says diagrams are DERIVED VIEWS of these matrices, so a hand-drawn one would be a second source of truth for the same facts. If a picture is wanted, it is rendered from the allocation and the edge set above, and the owner has an open design round on the state-machine renderer where that belongs.
